_readme: BOOT DESCRIPTOR — /etc/rip-cage/boot.json (ADR-031 D4). The one declarative
file init reads at boot. JSON, because jq is the base image's only parser and
init already depends on it; JSON has no comment syntax, so this _readme key IS
the header comment. Every reader ignores unknown keys.
SCHEMA — three optional top-level arrays; a listed field marked (req) missing or
empty makes init exit non-zero naming the field and the entry (ADR-001 fail-loud):
daemons[]      name (req)  start (req)  health (req)  state_dir
multiplexers[] name (req)  start (req)  attach (req)  exec  new_session  teardown
tools[]        name (req)  launch  init
Every start/health/attach/launch/init value is a shell command string, run
with `sh -c`. Multiplexer hooks receive the --session name as $1.
tools[].launch wraps how the tool STARTS (the base image bakes one generic
wrapper per agent binary; the entry supplies its command). tools[].init is a
one-shot agent-context hook run once at boot — no sudo, fail-warn.
DAEMON GOTCHA, carried verbatim from the manifest era (rip-cage-893l): init
backgrounds `start` and records $! as the daemon's PID. A start command that
does setup work before launching the server records the WRAPPER's pid, not the
daemon's — prefix the real server with `exec` so the recorded pid is the one
that serves. And nothing inside a cage reaps orphans (msb's PID 1 leaves an
exited daemon in state Z forever, where `kill -0` still succeeds), so `health`
— not the pid — is the liveness authority. See docs/reference/in-cage-daemon.md.
EXTENDING: your Dockerfile merges a fragment in with `rc-boot-merge <file>`.
rip-cage never edits this file for you — composition is yours (ADR-005 D12).
